correctness.rationale: Fourier differentiation and unit-step extremizer prove the exact finite sharp norm. Critical Fourier peaks have explicitly computed quartic and Gaussian expansions with a moving perturbation. Smooth cutoffs, local rescaling, fourth-derivative summable coefficient tails and an intermediate spatial radius establish uniform compact-parameter ℓ1 mass additivity; the fixed-u cases follow from single-peak localization. Exact finite convolution and independent FFT checks were executed, with finite checks not substituted for proof.

originality.rationale: The arXiv:1205.6490 full primary text (Proposition 2.4, Example 2.2) already constructs this exact five-tap symbol, locates the critical quartic and Gaussian peaks and proves fixed-parameter local limits. arXiv:1212.4700 further develops such local limits. The new theorem instead proves a global sharp BV/ℓ1 operator norm under the moving parameter 1/8+lambda/r and shows asymptotic additivity of the two physically separated scales; no checked prior statement supplies this varying-parameter norm. Residual uncertainty from unindexed prior stability work is recorded.
residual_risks: The 2012 Diaconis–Saloff-Coste work treats exactly the same multiplier and both Fourier peaks; the new global ℓ1 result is closely related and may be derivable by further arguments not stated there.
Older Schoenberg, Greville, Thomée and parabolic-difference stability literature may contain equivalent moving-parameter ℓ1 norm formulas that were not accessible in full.
The original 1964 paper was available as parsed PDF text, but page-image inspection was unavailable due to access restrictions.

value.rationale: The critical value u=1/8 is a canonical high-order lattice-diffusion stability edge. The sharp norm controls perturbations of finite-variation data, whereas earlier local limit theorems control pointwise kernel shape. The 1/r moving-parameter width and e^(16 lambda) profile expose a nontrivial second Fourier packet whose contribution survives in total variation although it is invisible at leading pointwise order.
